Total return with dividends from EUR 231.40; value per share includes dividends received. Italic cells are derived from the memo's per-turn values and bear FY2029 EPS of about EUR 12.5 (see end notes); the rest are the memo's own figures.

The skew: roughly balanced over 18 months, positive over three years. Over 18 months the distribution of price outcomes around the guideline is roughly balanced: the operating lines skew positive, the per-share consensus and sector sentiment skew negative, and the two resolve in opposite order. Over three years the skew is positive, because the de-rating is a one-off and the earnings compounding is not. A holder who accepts a flat multiple earns 8% to 9% a year and keeps an option worth 6% to 8% per turn of re-rating.

The base return has three modest requirements: data-centre orders normalising rather than pausing in 2027; positive net price in 2027; and PTC closing and deleveraging on schedule, so that the buyback restarts in 2029.

Counter-case. The de-rating can arrive in price terms before any of the earnings arrive. Consensus EPS is 6 to 7% above ours, and a market that values the stock on consensus and then watches consensus fall can deliver the fall at a constant multiple (a 6% EPS cut is −6% on the price). The three-year return also depends on 2028 and 2029 earnings, which sit in the wider range of outcomes.

What would change my view. Upward: the February backlog and guide confirming organic growth above 10% for 2027, which would lift the earnings path and strengthen the case for 16.5x. Downward: a dollar at 1.20 EUR/USD combined with net price near zero, which would take FY2027 EPS towards EUR 11.0 and the 18-month return at the guideline below zero.

Versus the market. The mean target price of EUR 328.68 (+42%) is in effect the 75th-percentile multiple applied to EPS that has not yet been cut; it is an outcome, not a base case. My base is the model's: mid-single-digit returns over 18 months at the guideline, low double digits at my multiple, and about 8% to 14% a year over three years depending on the multiple, all of it from earnings.

Conclusion: at the guideline multiple the shares return about +5% to December 2027 (dividends) and about +24% to June 2029 (+8.5% a year, all earnings), and every turn of multiple above 15.34x adds 6% to 8%, so the return is a bet on booked earnings with the multiple as the option.

Score: 40, set by the Rater. About +5%, almost all dividends, maps to about 37 in the D band; I lift it a little because the three-year check is +24% (8.5% a year, all earnings) and the Analyst's own 16.5x gives +13%, but hold it in D because the lower tail is fat (-13% at the 10th-percentile multiple, -27% on bear EPS) and consensus EPS is set to fall first.

13Summary conclusion on the business and the investment case

The business: a high-quality, asset-light electrical franchise in a peak operating year. Schneider has the strongest external demand in its history, an operating reset that is ahead of its own five-year plan, and two years of order-backed visibility.

Operating profit will, with high probability, do what the model says for FY2027: revenue up about 12%, adjusted EBITA up about 19%, and a margin above 20%.

What reaches each share is 6 to 7% less than consensus counts, for reasons that are already facts: 25m new shares, a 4.3% coupon and a Q4 2027 PTC closing. The market will learn this between the December 2026 consensus collection and the February 2027 results, before it learns about the H1 2027 margin and the July 2027 guidance raise.

Two forces set the multiple, and delivery can close only one of them. The first is the sector's fear about the financing of the AI build-out. The second, since October 2026, is a company-specific discount for an expensive, leveraged software acquisition. Delivery can close the second discount but not the first.

The return is modest over 18 months and respectable over three years at the guideline multiple, entirely from earnings. At any multiple nearer the stock's own median, the 18-month return is in the teens.

The case has three genuine fragilities. The first is a financing-led pause in data-centre orders during 2027, which would be a 2028 earnings event and would show first in credit markets and peers. The second is a turn in currency and metals prices. The third is the 2028 convergence of normalisation, the capacity wave, full PTC consolidation and peak interest.

The practical conclusion. The operating evidence improves through July 2027; the per-share and sentiment evidence gets worse first; and the window in which both point the same way opens between the February and July 2027 results. 2027 is the cleaner year of a two-year holding, and the 2028 debate will arrive before the recovery is old.

2027 is the clean year; in 2028 normalisation, the capacity wave, full PTC consolidation and peak interest land together.

2027: the cleaner year

  • Revenue mostly in the backlog (Q2–Q3 2026 data-centre orders convert over 12–24 months)
  • Price carry-over peaks in H1 2027: about +EUR 400m net
  • Restructuring falls EUR 450m → 250m
  • Only one quarter of PTC; organic growth 10.5%
  • Overhead ratio still falling at 10% growth

2028: four things land together

  • Data-centre normalisation; organic growth 8.0%
  • The capacity wave fades price
  • Full PTC consolidation and integration
  • Peak interest: net financial items −EUR 1,480m
  • The undemonstrated strengths take over from the demonstrated ones

Thesis's Change Forces' Strength
78

Foundations' Robustness
79

Foundations' Robustness: 79, set by the Rater. A top-two franchise in concentrated, certification-gated, margin-first markets with a widening moat, about 100% cash conversion, an A rating and margins that held through 2009 and 2020 gives the stability Richard rewards (CVS Group and Arteche 80), with an operating delivery record of floors cleared and raises; kept just below 80 by below-average capital allocation, mediocre returns on recently deployed capital and leverage rising to 2.3x.

Setups' Fit/Crispness
74

Setups' Fit/Crispness: 74, set by the Rater. The case fits Demand-driven EPS Upgrader in substance: structural demand, capacity grown fourfold and a record of delivery lift the EPS growth rate from 7% to about 15%; one current problem blurs it, the PTC deal with its dilution, peak leverage and buyback pause, which weakens the per-share step-up. I do not count the multiple at its ten-year median or the consensus still to be reset, which the memo's C weighed, so I sit above its grade at the 75 level for a clear fit with one current problem.

Case Riskiness
58

Case Riskiness: 58, set by the Rater. The operating case is simple and largely booked for 18 months, but like Richard's Arteche 60 the main risk of a large share-price fall is a theme-carried price (AI-infrastructure financing), here compounded by leverage peaking at 2.3x, a 2028 in which four negatives land together and an EPS consensus set to fall first, so it sits slightly below topic 9's 60.

How to read this page

Every rating of this stock on one page: the Rater's 1-100 number, its letter and the Rater's own reason (at most three sentences, taken from the ratings file; nothing newly written). The number is the company's approximate standing in the Universe of about 1,300 listed European companies (90 = better than about 9 in 10; 50 = typical). A letter follows its item's rule: rank among the stocks scored (A the top 10%; B+ and B the next 15%; C+, C and C- the next 25%; D the next 25%; F the bottom 25%); or Richard's cut-offs on the measure for the four numerical topics (forecast financials, current momentum, the fair multiple, total shareholder return). On the change-forces items the number carries a sign (50 = neither positive nor negative) and the letter is the rank, so read the two together. "9th of 30 stocks scored" is the stock's place on that item. A dashed badge is provisional (fewer than 30 stocks scored).
